plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant blossoms open on bare branches while winter still grips the landscape. Each flower is a delicate five-petaled cup, and whole orchards haze over in pink and white. Their sweet, spicy perfume drifts on the cold air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, usually peaking in mid-February
plants.location: Japan, including the Mito and Atami plum gardens, and across eastern China
plants.funFact: Ume blooms are traditionally seen as the first herald of spring in East Asia, arriving weeks before cherry blossoms. The fruit is pickled as umeboshi or steeped into plum wine.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom in the protea family looks like a crown of silky, pointed pink bracts around a downy center. It stands boldly among fynbos shrubs, and its flowerheads can reach the size of a dinner plate.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom runs from late spring through summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowers also appearing in February in some areas
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its tough, fire-adapted rootstock lets it resprout after the wildfires that regularly sweep the fynbos.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs burst into rose-like blooms in the cool months, with layered petals and golden stamens set against dark green leaves. They are a favorite for brightening winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with a mid-February peak in many regions
plants.location: Southeastern United States (such as Georgia and the Carolinas), Japan, and mild climates worldwide
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Japanese gardens have grown it for centuries, and it has thousands of named cultivars.
